clean_source_blocks.text: More people rescued from flooded Laos cave on Saturday after more than a week Some of those freed from a flooded cave in Laos are helping in efforts to find the last two missing men trapped inside, rescuers have said. So far, five of the seven initially missing have been rescued but it is believed the remaining two men are trapped deeper inside the cave in the mountain area of central Xaysomboun province. The men, all local villagers, entered the narrow tunnels on 20 May in search of gold but flash floods stopped them from leaving. On Sunday, a rescuer told AFP that several survivors were giving advice from their hospital room on how to find the remaining men, including descriptions of the deeper part of the cave.

Some of those freed from a flooded cave in Laos are helping in efforts to find the last two missing men trapped inside, rescuers have said. So far, five of the seven initially missing have been rescued but it is believed the remaining two men are trapped deeper inside the cave in the mountain area of central Xaysomboun province. The men, all local villagers, entered the narrow tunnels on 20 May in search of gold but flash floods stopped them from leaving. On Sunday, a rescuer told AFP that several survivors were giving advice from their hospital room on how to find the remaining men, including descriptions of the deeper part of the cave.
So far, five men have been freed from the narrow, flooded cave but efforts are ongoing to locate two more.

Yoshitaka Isaji said the passage used in rescue efforts on Saturday was currently impassable because a drainage pump had broken, but repair efforts were ongoing. Earlier in the week, a plan to pump out flood water from the tunnels also failed. Specialist divers from other countries including Thailand, Indonesia, France and Australia are also helping the searches. The first man was freed by rescuers on Friday. original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Some of those freed from a flooded cave in Laos are helping in efforts to find the last two missing men trapped inside, rescuers have said.

So far, five of the seven initially missing have been rescued but it is believed the remaining two men are trapped deeper inside the cave in the mountain area of central Xaysomboun province.

The men, all local villagers, entered the narrow tunnels on 20 May in search of gold but flash floods stopped them from leaving.

On Sunday, a rescuer told AFP that several survivors were giving advice from their hospital room on how to find the remaining men, including descriptions of the deeper part of the cave.

A Laotian rescue group said the men's information on the cave system - which extends deep underground and in some places measures around 50cm (20in) wide - was "considered substantial" and used in preparing a new search plan.

A fresh effort to find the remaining two men was expected on Sunday.

It comes as reports said the four men who left the cave on Saturday managed to free themselves without the help of rescuers after the water level lowered.

One unverified video posted to social media showed cheers from both rescuers and onlookers as the men emerged from the cave.

It was not clear what caused the water to lower, but a Japanese rescue diver told AP on Sunday that flood water was being drained from the cave.

Yoshitaka Isaji said the passage used in rescue efforts on Saturday was currently impassable because a drainage pump had broken, but repair efforts were ongoing.

Earlier in the week, a plan to pump out flood water from the tunnels also failed.

Specialist divers from other countries including Thailand, Indonesia, France and Australia are also helping the searches.

The first man was freed by rescuers on Friday.

More people rescued from flooded Laos cave on Saturday after more than a week

Some of those freed from a flooded cave in Laos are helping in efforts to find the last two missing men trapped inside, rescuers have said.

So far, five of the seven initially missing have been rescued but it is believed the remaining two men are trapped deeper inside the cave in the mountain area of central Xaysomboun province.

The men, all local villagers, entered the narrow tunnels on 20 May in search of gold but flash floods stopped them from leaving.

On Sunday, a rescuer told AFP that several survivors were giving advice from their hospital room on how to find the remaining men, including descriptions of the deeper part of the cave.

A Laotian rescue group said the men's information on the cave system - which extends deep underground and in some places measures around 50cm (20in) wide - was "considered substantial" and used in preparing a new search plan.

A fresh effort to find the remaining two men was expected on Sunday.

It comes as reports said the four men who left the cave on Saturday managed to free themselves without the help of rescuers after the water level lowered.

One unverified video posted to social media showed cheers from both rescuers and onlookers as the men emerged from the cave.

It was not clear what caused the water to lower, but a Japanese rescue diver told AP on Sunday that flood water was being drained from the cave.

Yoshitaka Isaji said the passage used in rescue efforts on Saturday was currently impassable because a drainage pump had broken, but repair efforts were ongoing.

Earlier in the week, a plan to pump out flood water from the tunnels also failed.

Specialist divers from other countries including Thailand, Indonesia, France and Australia are also helping the searches.

The first man was freed by rescuers on Friday.

[Lähde: The Guardian]
Video appears to show divers discovering group sitting on a rock surrounded by flood water

Rescuers have reached five of seven people who have been trapped for a week in a flooded, remote cave in Laos, after days spent navigating narrow, inundated passageways amid persistent rain.

Video footage shared on social media by rescue divers showed the five men crouched together on a rocky ledge in a dark cave chamber, surrounded by muddy water. “There’s no need to cry,” one of the rescue team told the men, who first entered the cave on Wednesday. Two men remain unaccounted for.

When asked about their health, the men told the rescuers they were hungry and dehydrated.

Outside, rescuers jumped up and down in joy, hugging one another after learning the group had been located. A boy, among families desperately waiting for news, spotted his father in the group and raised his hands in a gesture of gratitude. “I am happy for you, son,” a member of the rescue team responded.

“What a feeling,” wrote Mikko Paasi, a Finnish diver, on social media after he was filmed reaching the men along with Norrased Palasing, a Thai diver. But he added: “This is only a brief relief as the five survivors are still in the terminal chamber, all healthy and in good spirits, but the extraction is still ahead and it ain’t going to be easy.”

The group reportedly entered the cave in Xaysomboun province, central Laos, to hunt for wildlife and search for gold, but heavy rain blocked the cave entrance.

Thai and international divers, including Paasi , who helped in the dramatic rescue of a young Thai football team in 2018, travelled to Laos to help bring the men to safety.

For days, teams had been battling to reach a terminal chamber about 300 metres (984ft) from the cave entrance, crawling and climbing through tunnels that were at times just 60cm (24in) deep. Passageways were almost completely filled with water and sediment. On Tuesday, the team had focused on reinforcing safety measures, and installing internet cables in the cave so that the team could monitor the situation and relay first-aid advice quickly if necessary.

payload.title: Laosissa luolasta pelastetut auttavat kahden kadonneen etsinnässä
payload.summary: Viisi seitsemästä Laosissa tulvaluolaan loukkuun jääneestä miehestä on saatu pelastettua, ja osa selviytyneistä auttaa nyt etsijöitä sairaalasta käsin. Kaksi miestä uskotaan yhä olevan syvemmällä luolastossa.
payload.content:
Viisi miestä on pelastettu kapeasta ja tulvaveden täyttämästä luolasta Laosissa, mutta kahden muun etsinnät jatkuvat edelleen Keski-Laosin vuoristoalueella. Pelastajien mukaan osa luolasta ulos saaduista miehistä auttaa nyt etsintätyötä sairaalasta käsin kuvailemalla luolaston syvempiä osia ja mahdollisia reittejä kadonneiden löytämiseksi.

## Miehet jäivät loukkuun äkkitulvan vuoksi

Seitsemän paikallista kyläläistä meni luolaan 20. toukokuuta etsimään kultaa. He eivät päässeet enää ulos, kun äkkitulvat täyttivät kapeita tunneleita vedellä. Pelastustöitä on tehty yli viikon ajan Xaysombounin maakunnassa Keski-Laosin vuoristoalueella.

Pelastajien mukaan viisi miehistä on tähän mennessä saatu ulos. Ensimmäinen heistä pelastettiin perjantaina, ja lisää miehiä saatiin turvaan lauantaina. Kahden jäljellä olevan uskotaan olevan syvemmällä luolassa, mikä tekee etsinnästä vaikeaa ja vaarallista.

Sunnuntaina pelastaja kertoi, että useat selviytyneet ovat antaneet sairaalahuoneestaan neuvoja etsijöille. Heidän tietonsa voivat olla tärkeitä, koska luolaston sisäosista on niukasti varmaa tietoa ja olosuhteet ovat muuttuneet tulvaveden takia.

## Rikkoutunut pumppu vaikeuttaa etenemistä

Pelastustöitä on hidastanut myös kalustoon liittyvä ongelma. Yoshitaka Isajin mukaan lauantaina käytetty kulkureitti oli toistaiseksi poissa käytöstä, koska vedenpoistopumppu oli rikkoutunut. Pumpun korjaamista jatkettiin, mutta aiempi yritys pumpata tulvavettä tunneleista ei ollut onnistunut.

Etsintöihin osallistuu myös erikoissukeltajia useista maista, kuten Thaimaasta, Indonesiasta, Ranskasta ja Australiasta. Heidän apuaan tarvitaan, koska luola on kapea, osin veden täyttämä ja paikoin vaikeakulkuinen.

Viranomaisten ja pelastajien keskeinen tavoite on paikantaa kaksi edelleen kateissa olevaa miestä mahdollisimman nopeasti. Selviytyneiden kertomukset luolan syvemmistä kohdista voivat auttaa rajaamaan etsintäaluetta, mutta vedenpinnan, rikkoutuneen pumppukaluston ja luolaston ahtauden vuoksi eteneminen on yhä hidasta.

Osa selviytyneistä neuvoo pelastajia sairaalasta käsin kuvailemalla luolan sisäosia.
